entries.core_move: Compute $p(t)=|x(t)|^2$ from a continuous-time signal $x(t)$ and interpret it as the pointwise signal-size quantity that underlies energy and average-power calculations.

Convert instantaneous signal power into signal energy by integrating $|x(t)|^2$ over all time and interpreting finite or infinite totals as the signal-size basis for later energy, decaying-signal, and power classifications.

Compute the energy of a finite-duration continuous-time signal by using its support to set finite integration bounds, squaring its magnitude, and evaluating the resulting definite integral or piecewise sum.

Compute total energy for decaying continuous-time signals by squaring the signal magnitude, setting the correct semi-infinite integration limits, and evaluating the resulting convergent improper integral.

Compute average signal power for a continuous-time signal by evaluating the symmetric long-time average of $|x(t)|^2$ and interpreting the value as sustained signal size distinct from finite total energy.
Compute the power of a periodic continuous-time signal by converting the average-power limit into $P=\frac{1}{T_0}\int_{t_0}^{t_0+T_0}|x(t)|^2\,dt$ over any fundamental period.

Classify continuous-time signals as energy signals, power signals, or neither by using total energy and time-average power calculations to apply the finite-energy, finite-nonzero-power, and neither-case criteria in the Signal Size module.
